doc.title: Red Holloway interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995

title: Making a Bill Cosby LP in four hours
summary: They recorded a whole album with Cosby directing parts verbally with no written music.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: It could be C minor, or C7 or whatever, it wouldn’t be no diminished this. But it was really, it was really nice. In fact there was one other period I made a record with and we went in and to show you how things can be done, now this was we were in the studio with Bill Cosby. And I made an LP with him. We made an LP in about 4 hours and 20 minutes. And we had no idea what he was going to play, and what he was gonna— there was no music, he’d tell the drummer to play me this beat [scats]. And he’d tell the bass

player what to play. He say, “Now Red, you play” [scats]. Then he would have the drummer to fill up the rhythm and the other horns and the guitar, he’d give you all your parts, and then we’d play that for maybe a couple of choruses, then he’d change it around, so it would take us maybe, it would take us maybe of 20 minutes to get a song together, then we’d record it. We’d play it twice. Three times at the most. And that was it. But I mean he had all this in his head. He knew what he wanted to do, he didn’t have the music because he didn’t know nothing about writing any music, but Bill Cosby played a little drums, so he knew the rhythms and things, and he could sing. And we recorded a whole album, Yeah.
